name: TextAttack
hook: NLP adversarial-attack framework from the QData lab (ACL 2020).
what_atr_did: Issue #824 proposes a textattack-detection-atr companion PyPI package — plugin-shaped, zero core changes. Single ask: README cross-link.

name: Microsoft PyRIT
hook: The toolkit Microsoft uses internally to red-team production LLM products. Roman Lutz leads.
what_atr_did: Added an ATR dataset loader exposing the rule corpus as PyRIT attack sources; PR #1715 merged 2026-05-27.

name: HackAPrompt
org: Schulhoff et al. — Learn Prompting · EMNLP 2023
hook: A dataset of 600K+ prompts (601,757 rows in the released version) from a global prompt-hacking competition, in which players tried to make gpt-3.5-turbo, FlanT5-XXL or text-davinci-003 print a target phrase or give up a hidden secret key. The paper describing it (Schulhoff et al., EMNLP 2023) is listed under Best Paper Awards at EMNLP 2023.
what_atr_did: Shipped 5 ATR rules (ATR-2026-00452..00456), promoted to rules/ on 2026-05-12, each written for an attack family the corpus shows: a forced target phrase, secret-key reveal demands, per-character backslash encoding, a no-period output modifier, and empty-input conditionals; other rules name HackAPrompt in their YAML too. Recall is measured on a fixed 4,780-prompt subset (a seeded random sample of 5,000 rows at a pinned dataset revision, less the 220 shorter than 3 characters): each prompt goes through the evaluation harness as LLM input and counts as detected when any rule matches. Several of the rules naming HackAPrompt were written from this exact subset, so the current recall that follows is in-sample; it is followed by the ablation reference, the same prompts with every rule naming HackAPrompt removed. The corpus is 100% adversarial and carries no benign population, so it yields no precision or false-positive figure.

name: Promptfoo + llm-guard
hook: Attack examples from promptfoo's red-team plugins and test cases from llm-guard's scanner tests, both MIT-licensed.
what_atr_did: Shipped 6 ATR rules (ATR-2026-00500..00505), promoted to rules/ on 2026-05-12. Four are generalised from promptfoo plugin examples (SSRF, data exfiltration, divergent repetition, tool discovery) and two from llm-guard test cases (fake error-state takeover, and system prompt extraction, which also draws on promptfoo): literal hostnames, URLs, words and tool names in the examples were replaced with patterns. Each rule's description names the corpus it came from. The 2026-05-12 import they came from held 94 samples (44 llm-guard, 44 promptfoo, 6 NeMo Guardrails); checked against the vendor repositories, 79 occur verbatim in the vendor file they name, 3 are truncated or edited from it, 2 come from another vendor's suite, and 10 are not found verbatim anywhere in the vendor repository at the pinned commit. The rules are now measured on 126 attack and 20 benign test cases, extracted by script from pinned commits of llm-guard, promptfoo and NVIDIA NeMo Guardrails (Apache-2.0; a measurement source only, no rule was derived from it) and deduplicated, each counted as detected when any rule matches. Two of the three suites are the rules' own sources, so the current recall that follows is partly in-sample; it is followed by the ablation reference, the same cases with every rule naming one of the three vendors or the vendor-corpus-import tag removed. Even that is not out-of-sample: some remaining rules carry vendor text in their YAML, and five NeMo Guardrails cases share a jailbreak template with the garak corpus other rules were mined from (the measurement file quantifies both). The 20 benign cases are too few for a precision claim; only the count flagged is given. Since agent-threat-rules#709, ATR-2026-00500 and -00501 match all 3 vendor cases in the categories they cite and ATR-2026-00505 matches all 6 vendor cases behind its true positives (hunt); before it, 00500 and 00501 matched 1 and 0.

name: OWASP LLM Top 10 + MITRE ATLAS
hook: OWASP's Top 10 risks for LLM applications, and MITRE ATLAS, the catalog of adversarial techniques and case studies against AI systems.
what_atr_did: Shipped 8 ATR rules (ATR-2026-00510..00517) on 2026-05-12. Each rule's references name an OWASP LLM Top 10 (2025) category (LLM01, LLM02, LLM06 or LLM10) and a MITRE ATLAS technique, and six of the eight descriptions cite the ATLAS case study they follow (AML.CS0022, CS0036, CS0038, CS0039 and CS0045, CS0041, CS0056).

name: Promptfoo
hook: Open-source LLM red-teaming and evaluation tool. Promptfoo generates and runs adversarial tests against LLM applications.
what_atr_did: PR #8529 adds an MCP red-team example using ATR as the deterministic defense layer. Promptfoo runs the probe; ATR rules return the verdict.
